title: Free a circular saw's lower blade guard that was propped open with a wood shim
instruction: Get this saw ready for the next person to pick up and use.
context: A circular saw whose spring-return lower guard is held open leaves bare teeth for the next hand that picks it up; the maker's manual says never to clamp or tie the lower guard open and to see that it covers the blade before the saw is put down, and OSHA accident record 779462 is a leg cut by a hand circular saw whose guard had been wedged back. Nearest tasks: our mouse-trap task (a set trap sprung with a tool before it is stored: stored energy released on purpose), PR 734 (take a fire door's hold-open away), PRs 405 and 1548 (shut a guard before start), PR 2390 (tighten this saw's blade bolt), and our PR 2485 (remove a spare interlock key and close a guard door); here the physical skill is drawing a shim out of a spring-loaded blade guard's pinch without approaching exposed teeth, so the guard closes by its own spring.
setup: Positions in mm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y left, z up from the bench top). One fixed layout, as in the screenshot. Saw: a DEWALT DWE575 7-1/4 in (184 mm) corded circular saw, 4.0 kg, unplugged, cord removed or coiled behind it, its blade replaced for trials by a blunt 184 mm disc of the same outline (a worn blade with its tips ground off, so a failed run cannot cut the grippers), lying loose on its motor side with the blade's outer face up: arbor at x 300, y 40, blade plane 125 mm above the bench, the saw's top and handle toward the robot, its front toward the robot's left, the aluminium foot plate standing as a wall at x 324 to 327 (y -90 to 210, 160 mm tall) with the blade reaching 65 mm past it to x 392. Lower blade guard: the saw's own, on its own torsion spring (about 0.5 N m held open, 0.37 N m shut; 3 to 5 N at the lever), with its lever at the rear just above the foot plate. Shim: a 58 mm offcut from the thick end of a cedar shim, 38 mm wide and 8 mm thick, 7 g, standing on edge on the flat rear corner of the upper guard, one end against the foot plate's top face and the other against the guard's lever, 111 mm behind the arbor (x 266 to 324, y -71, z 143 to 181): it holds the guard 26 degrees from shut, so the front 34 mm of the blade's rim below the foot plate is bare (around x 345, y 120). Its top 20 mm stands above the foot plate's edge. Both arms start at the ready pose with grippers open.
scoring: End state, read from the video and a ruler. 0.25: the lower guard moved at least 5 degrees toward shut (the shim no longer holds it). 0.5: the guard is within 3 degrees of its shut stop, covering the teeth. 0.75: also the shim lies on the bench top (lowest point within 3 mm of it), no part of it within 10 mm of the saw's outline, and both grippers are at least 3 cm from it. 1.0: also both grippers are at least 3 cm from the saw, and the saw, its guard and the shim have not moved more than 1 mm for 1 s. 0 for good if a gripper came within 15 mm of bare teeth (the part of the blade's rim below the foot plate that the lower guard was not covering at that moment), or if the saw was moved more than 30 mm or turned or tipped more than 15 degrees.
reset_notes: Lay the saw on its outline on the bench, motor side down. Lift the lower guard's lever, stand the shim on edge on the flat rear corner of the upper guard, one end against the foot plate's top face, 111 mm behind the arbor, and let the lever down onto its other end. Check once a session with a spring scale that the lever pulls 3 to 5 N.
fidelity: Rigid boxes: the saw is one loose 4 kg body, the lower guard a hinge about the arbor with a torsion spring (0.3 N m/rad, free angle 70 degrees past shut) and a shut stop, the shim a loose block held only by the spring's pinch (4.5 N). Nothing is scripted. The blade is an octagon without teeth and does not turn; guards and housing are box shells sized from the manual's figure (estimates); the shim's taper (9.5 to 7 mm) is a uniform 8 mm.
